prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: parking lot collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1112; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer narrative, parking lot collision, Katy, Texas. Driver 1 was backing out of a stall when the rear bumper of Driver 1's vehicle made contact with the front quarter panel of Driver 2's vehicle, which was stopped in the adjacent lane. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. The Passenger, seated in the front right position of Driver 1's vehicle, reported pain in the right shoulder at the scene and was transported for evaluation. The Passenger's account of the impact and the reported shoulder injury are consistent with the force and direction of the collision. Damage to both vehicles lines up with the described impact, and photographs taken at the scene confirm the positions of the vehicles and the points of contact. No prior damage to either vehicle has been identified. Both the responding officer and the drivers confirmed the Passenger was inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. No independent witnesses were located in the lot, so the account relies on the statements of those involved and the physical evidence recorded at the scene.
